problem: Prior explicit-prediction ObjectNav methods predict from single-view egocentric context (SSCNav, L2M) or predict frontier potential functions (PONI), which depend heavily on unseen obstacles and are hard to estimate accurately. End-to-end RL/IL methods need huge data and compute and lack interpretability.
motivation: Efficient ObjectNav requires spatial and semantic layout priors and reasoning about uncertainty in unexplored areas. The authors argue the global semantic map from all past observations is the right context, and that directly predicting target locations decouples goal prediction from obstacle prediction, making it learnable from little data.
key_idea: Train a lightweight PSPNet on passively collected incomplete semantic maps to directly predict per-category target-object probability in unexplored areas from the global map, then choose long-term goals via a distance-weighted argmax and navigate with an analytical planner (no RL).
insight: Global context matters: the same network trained on egocentric crops gives worse predictions (DTO 1.974 vs 1.518; NLL 9.460 vs 8.873 for global). In navigation ablation on HM3D val, removing predictions drops SPL from 0.320 to 0.235 and success from 0.638 to 0.478, and removing distance weighting costs a little (0.310 / 0.598). Ground-truth segmentation raises performance to 0.400 SPL / 0.756 success, showing perception is the main bottleneck.
method: Semantic mapping: SemExp-style top-down map (N+4 channels: obstacle, explored, current/past position, target and other categories) built from RGB-D segmentation and depth projected with pose, 5 cm resolution, 960x960.

Unseen object probability prediction: PSPNet (ResNet50) takes the whole global map and outputs C-channel target probabilities, trained with BCE to predict zero on explored areas; ground truth comes from the step-500 map.

Training data generation: an exploration agent (Stubborn baseline) wanders 500 steps from 50 start locations per scene; maps saved every 25 steps, steps 25-250 used as inputs; augmentation with rotation, flip, padded-crop.

Goal selection: weight the probability map by exp(-d/λ) using geodesic (Fast Marching) distance on the known obstacle map (optimistic in unexplored areas), λ=5 m, take argmax as the long-term goal; update every 10 steps or when the goal is reached.
Analytical local policy: Fast Marching shortest path to the goal, waypoint extraction, replanning each step, and Stubborn-style recovery when stuck.
Segmentation: Mask-RCNN fine-tuned on 100K HM3D images (6 goal + 3 extra categories) for HM3D; RedNet for MP3D (21 categories).

setting.backbone: PSPNet (ResNet50) map predictor trained supervised; Mask-RCNN (HM3D) / RedNet (MP3D) segmenters; analytical Fast Marching planner
setting.training_data: Semantic maps from passive exploration in the benchmark's own training scenes only: 4000 train/1000 val sequences on HM3D, 2800/550 on MP3D; Mask-RCNN fine-tuned on 80K+20K HM3D images (COCO-pretrained). Trained under one GPU day.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, HFOV 79°) plus noiseless pose (x,y,θ)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.privileged: none (noiseless GPS+compass pose as per the standard ObjectNav setup; GT segmentation only in an ablation)

results: PEANUT reaches 0.33 SPL / 0.64 success on HM3D test-standard, beating ProcTHOR (0.32 SPL, which uses extra synthetic data) and OVRL (0.60 success). On MP3D val it gets the best SPL (0.158 vs Stubborn 0.149) with success 0.405, matching Stubborn's 0.407 and beating PONI (0.121 / 0.227).
limitations: Heavily dependent on semantic segmentation quality; GT segmentation lifts success from 0.638 to 0.756.
Single top-down 2D map cannot handle multi-floor scenes; stairs are marked as obstacles so the agent gets stuck.
Prediction uses only the semantic map (no RGB or 3D geometry) and assumes noiseless pose; MP3D test-standard was not evaluated.
